acceptanceCriteria: Capture a reproducible identity-bound baseline and candidate for status warm startup, medium repository observation, and one Work Item verification route; report samples, median, filesRead/filesHashed, gitCalls, executed/reused nodes, workers, and elapsedMs without claiming provider or enterprise performance.

Reduce measured Rust Runtime cost through request-scoped reuse, bounded memoization, or equivalent Rust-native changes while preserving repository isolation, snapshot identity, Contract semantics, required gates, evidence binding, and fail-closed behavior; a Git snapshot must not re-enumerate the same source tree for its derived digest.

The performance fixture reaches the documented status <50 ms and observation <100 ms targets on the declared local platform, or records an explicit bounded gap and fails the performance gate rather than weakening governance; no unmeasured speedup claim is accepted.
Repeated requests for the same repository snapshot reuse only matching identity-bound observations/verification results; changed or unknown inputs execute the declared checks and record the reason.

Independent Work Items may execute in parallel only with disjoint repository scopes and receive separate Work Item evidence receipts; no cross-Work-Item receipt or global current-repository state is introduced.

Performance regression, repository isolation, lifecycle, and full workspace tests pass; tri-language performance documentation states the installation boundary as shared external Runtime plus explicit --repo and does not copy reference installers, Make/Python, SDK, or V1 runtime behavior.
Adopter-facing performance guidance and acceptance steps are reproducible with the published/installed Runtime and preserve per-repository Runtime and evidence identities.
goal: Push Rust Runtime execution efficiency toward the measured limits without weakening governance or object-project inheritance.
intent: Establish a measured, Rust-native performance optimization tranche for request-scoped status, observation, and verification reuse while preserving fail-closed governance and object-project inheritance.
outOfScope: Changing verification truth, Outcome state/marker semantics, Contract authority, required evidence, or fail-closed decisions to obtain speed.
Removing required CI, Windows, V1 oracle, provider, security, or enterprise checks; adding environment-variable bypasses or global caches.
Copying or porting the reference installer, Make/Python runtime, SDK/toolchain installation, legacy wire schema, or business-project code.
Repository-global current project state, cross-repository cache sharing, release packaging, Homebrew, and the next reference-file parity batch.
A broad lib.rs architecture split or scheduler/dependency-graph redesign unless a measured bottleneck and a separately authorized bounded amendment are recorded.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Repeated status and observe requests for an unchanged repository snapshot meet the declared local budgets through identity-bound reuse without changing facts.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Capture before/after samples with the performance fixture and verify snapshot, repository, Runtime, and profile identities for every reuse decision.

scenarioCoverage.expected: A changed tree, Contract, policy, command, or unknown impact never reuses stale results and instead executes or stops with a stable reason.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run mutation and unknown-impact regressions, inspect cost observations, and assert no stale evidence is accepted.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Independent disjoint scopes may run concurrently with bounded workers while each Work Item retains a separate identity-bound receipt and repository state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Exercise parallel verification/lifecycle tests across disjoint scopes and assert no cross-Work-Item or cross-repository receipt reuse.

scenarioCoverage.expected: The installed/published Runtime applies the same measured reuse semantics to an adopter repository using explicit --repo, without copying installers, SDKs, or Runtime source.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the isolated adopter performance smoke with the published binary and retain Runtime/repository identity and isolation evidence.

sources: Pinned reference performance semantics are advisory only; no installer or legacy runtime behavior is copied.
